title: Safety issue! Medtrum Nano pump (on-body) was reported falling back to priming stage after activation failed.
body:
Medtrum Nano **Safety problem?**

At least 2 users reported on Discord a situation where the Medtrum nano, while already on body with needle pressed, fell back to priming stage. As a result user was administered full priming insulin (which could be up-to 10 Units of insulin).

As it should not be possible to happen and can create life‑threatening situations Ik think this needs further investigation.

**Suggestions to test:**

A) _Using a nano Pod not on-body (or without inserting the needle)_
1. During Medtrum activation, make it fail
2. Then press "Cancel" instead of Retry?
3. Press Next
Does this maybe retrigger priming phase (while obviously, pump is then already onbody with needle inserted)?

comments.body:
Which AAPS version was used? 

Missing a lot of information here

Discord user here that reported the issue. 

When:
08 March 2026  (around 6 - 6:30 , pump time)

[AndroidAPS._2026-03-08_00-00-07_.1.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26352364/AndroidAPS._2026-03-08_00-00-07_.1.txt)

## What happened
- Normal activation: priming completed → patch attached → needle inserted  
- During final step, received an error (“activation failed”, exact wording unclear)  
- After pressing retry/back, the pump started priming again  
- This occurred while the patch was already inserted in the body  

## Outcome
- ~40 minutes later: glucose dropped from 180 → 20 mg/dL  
- AndroidAPS showed 0 IOB  
- Severe hypoglycemia symptoms (cold, sweating, unresponsive)  
- Treated with dextrose (glucagon not needed)  
- Estimated unintended insulin delivery: ~5–10 U  

## Expected
- No priming allowed when patch is already on-body  
- Or a clear instruction to discard the patch after activation failure  

## Actual
- System allowed re-priming without warning  
- No clear safety message shown  

## Device info
- Phone: Poco X3 NFC (Android 12, MIUI 14.0.5)  
- Pump: MD8201  
- Firmware: 1.80.83  
- AAPS version: 3.3.1.0  

## Notes
- Another user reported similar behavior  
- Logs attached  

## Suggestion
- Block re-priming if the patch is already inserted  
- Add a critical warning after activation failure  
- Prevent reuse or restart of patch activation

## Log Analysis — Root Cause Identified

I analyzed the attached log file (`AndroidAPS._2026-03-08_00-00-07_.1.txt`) and can confirm the re-priming happened. Here's the exact sequence:

### Timeline

| Time | Event |
|------|-------|
| 06:16:50 | **1st priming starts** (normal) |
| 06:19:22 | Priming complete → EJECTED. UI moves to ATTACH_PATCH |
| 06:20:24 | **BLE disconnects** while user is attaching patch |
| 06:20:28 | BLE reconnects — `SynchronizePacket` reports pump state as **FILLED** (not EJECTED) |
| 06:20:28 | SetupStep regresses: PRIMED → **FILLED** |
| 06:20:55 | User tries to activate — **fails** (pump is FILLED, not PRIMED) |
| 06:21:04–06:22:26 | **6 more activation retries, all fail** |
| 06:22:30 | User cancels |
| 06:22:37 | User enters **RETRY_ACTIVATION_CONNECT** flow |
| 06:22:40 | Reconnects — pump still reports **FILLED** |
| 06:22:42 | `MedtrumRetryActivationConnectFragment` sees FILLED → **`forceMoveStep(PatchStep.PRIME)`** |
| 06:22:43 | **2nd priming starts — patch is already on body with needle inserted** |
| 06:25:04 | 2nd priming completes (~2.5 min of insulin delivery into body) |
| 06:25:29 | Activation finally succeeds |

### Root Cause — Two issues combined

**1. BLE disconnect during ATTACH_PATCH causes state regression**

When BLE disconnected at 06:20:24 and reconnected at 06:20:28, the `SynchronizePacket` reported the pump state as `FILLED` instead of `EJECTED`/`PRIMED`. This caused the internal `SetupStep` to regress from `PRIMED` back to `FILLED`, making all subsequent activation attempts fail.

**2. Retry flow navigates to PRIME when it sees FILLED state**

In [`MedtrumRetryActivationConnectFragment.kt` line 39](https://github.com/nightscout/AndroidAPS/blob/master/pump/medtrum/src/main/kotlin/app/aaps/pump/medtrum/ui/MedtrumRetryActivationConnectFragment.kt#L39):
```kotlin
MedtrumViewModel.SetupStep.FILLED -> forceMoveStep(PatchStep.PRIME)
```

When the retry-activation flow sees `SetupStep.FILLED`, it assumes the patch was n
